---

### Synthesis Overview

This PR introduces a two-line null guard in `OutlineGenerator._index_story_analysis_chunk` and a focused two-test regression file. All three models independently agreed that the production fix is correct, minimal, and appropriate in scope. Agreement on the core verdict is unanimous. Divergence occurred only on minor test-file conventions — specifically whether the `sys.path.insert` pattern constitutes an anti-pattern — and on the significance of a narrow debug-branch coverage gap. Gemini's sole Warning finding is a false positive, as its factual premise (that pytest is already configured to auto-discover `src/`) is inconsistent with the actual `pyproject.toml` contents.

**Model Agreement Score:** 7/10

### Individual Report Summaries

| Model  | Overall Assessment       | Unique Focus Areas                         | Critical Count | Warning Count |
| ------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | -------------- | ------------- |
| Claude | Ready to merge           | Debug-branch coverage gap (minor)          | 0              | 0             |
| GPT    | Ready to merge (cleanest pass) | None — no findings of any kind        | 0              | 0             |
| Gemini | Ready to merge after fix | sys.path anti-pattern, test file structure | 0              | 1             |

**Claude** gave the most thorough structural review, examining all eight call sites, confirming correct guard placement, and noting that the `sys.path.insert` pattern is an established convention in the codebase (verified across seven other test files). Issued one low-priority suggestion regarding the uncovered debug branch.

**GPT** gave the cleanest pass of the three — no findings at any severity level. Assessment aligned with Claude on substantive correctness. Did not surface the debug-branch gap or the sys.path pattern.

**Gemini** was the only model to flag a Warning. It identified the `sys.path.insert` pattern as an anti-pattern on the premise that pytest already auto-discovers `src/` via `.toml` configuration. This premise is factually incorrect (see Divergence Analysis). Also suggested consolidating the test file into a general `test_outline_generator.py`, which does not exist.

### Divergence Analysis

```
[D-01] Topic: sys.path.insert in test files — anti-pattern or established convention?
Claude says: Established convention confirmed across seven test files in this project;
  not an issue introduced by this PR.
GPT says: Not mentioned (implicitly no concern).
Gemini says: Anti-pattern; pytest already auto-discovers src/ via pyproject.toml.
Assessment: Claude is correct. pyproject.toml does NOT configure `pythonpath`
  for pytest — it only sets `testpaths = ["tests/unit"]`. Without an explicit
  `pythonpath` entry, pytest does not add src/ to sys.path. The manual insertion
  is required for imports to resolve. This is a 2-vs-1 split (Claude + GPT silent
  vs. Gemini's incorrect assertion), and direct verification confirms Gemini's
  premise is wrong.
Resolution: Downgrade Gemini W-01 to False Positive. No action required.
```

```
[D-02] Topic: Suggestion count and test quality
Claude says: 1 minor suggestion (debug branch coverage).
GPT says: 0 suggestions; tests are complete.
Gemini says: 1 warning + 1 suggestion (both concerning test boilerplate/structure).
Assessment: All three agree the tests are logically sound and cover both branches
  of the main guard. The disagreement is on peripheral concerns only. Claude's
  debug-branch observation is the only substantive suggestion — it is real but
  low priority. Gemini's W-01 is false; GPT's silence is reasonable given the
  minor nature of the gap.
Resolution: Claude's S-C-01 noted as a genuine low-priority suggestion. No
  action required before merge.
```
